stem: While reconciling pharmacy records, a Xanax prescription issued five months ago has already been refilled five times. The patient asks for another refill. What should occur?

choices.text: Require renewed prescriber authorization because the federal five-refill limit has been reached.
Dispense a sixth refill because the prescription is still under six months old.
Treat the original notation as a practitioner renewal.
Use Massachusetts Schedule V rules instead of the federal Schedule IV rule.
Transfer the prescription to obtain five more refills.

explanation.core_reasoning: 'Require renewed prescriber authorization because the federal five-refill limit has been reached.' is the governing result. By contrast, 'Dispense a sixth refill because the prescription is still under six months old.' would require that the federal rule imposed only a time limit and no five-refill maximum. The decisive cue appears in 'While reconciling pharmacy records, a Xanax prescription issued five months ago has already been refilled five times. The patient asks for another refill. What should occur?'.

related_facts: alprazolam (Xanax) is used for anxiety disorder and panic disorder; it is federal Schedule IV and Massachusetts Schedule IV.
A Schedule III or IV prescription may not be filled or refilled more than six months after issue and may not be refilled more than five times unless renewed by the practitioner.
